# Independent adversarial audit: projective boundary potential and gauge erosion

Sources read in full:

* `candidate 85d2c2a949b59b29` (normalization dependency);
* `candidate 2d9458b5433d0a83`, Sections1–5;
* `candidate 4e871da0351ca07a`, Sections1–3, including the updated fixed-cover consequence.

Result: **PASS**. The ordinary boundary theorem and actual erosion are valid in every d>=1, with all stated nonsmooth and closed-halfspace cases. The mixed consequence is conditional on ACTUAL simultaneous compatibility and the displayed fixed covers. It proves no compatibility at tight anchored contacts and no general OC conclusion.

## Attainment and the ordinary normalization

The domain Omega is open and bounded because a ball rB lies in K. On compact subdomains its denominators have a common positive lower bound, so differentiating the volume integral is justified. The displayed Hessian is strictly positive in every nonzero direction because K has interior.

For a boundary sequence a_k, fix x_0 with1+a_0 dot x_0=0. The chosen disk in a_0-perp is genuinely transverse to x_0, so its cone has the asserted positive Jacobian proportional to t^(d-1). On the slab delta_k<=t<=2delta_k, the positive denominator is at most a constant times delta_k and the cone volume is at least a constant times delta_k^d. The volume lower bound c/delta_k is correct. The singleton-disk argument covers d=1. Thus a finite sublevel cannot approach the boundary of the bounded domain, and the strict convex minimum is attained in the interior. Its zero gradient is exactly the centroid of the projective image after the stated Jacobian substitution.

The projective map is used only for this ordinary body. Its positive denominators preserve oriented central halfspaces, convexity and ray order. No map is applied to the integer lattice or the full mixed family.

## Global continuation and boundary identity

The tangent-line extension of t^(-d) below delta is positive, finite, C1 and convex on the entire real line: the constant derivative below delta agrees with the increasing derivative above it. Thus h_K(n)f(1+a dot x) is a genuinely globally defined convex test in x, with continuous positive dependence on n. Its boundary integrals are finite and positive because the boundary is compact, the support distance is uniformly positive, and convex bodies have finite surface measure.

For F(x)=x/(1+a dot x)^d, I independently obtain

    div F=d/(1+a dot x)^(d+1).

The new cut face of K intersect H has zero flux for central H. Its intersection with the old boundary has zero (d-1)-measure: a point in the relative interior of the central section cannot lie on boundary K, since that would make its supporting normal perpendicular to the section and make the central plane support K, contradicting0 in int K. Hence only the section's relative boundary is involved. The d=1 cutting point misses the original endpoints. Gauss–Green on the bounded convex Lipschitz domains therefore gives the exact cap identity without discarding positive boundary mass.

Defect's independent radial identity gives the same result. The radial map is Lipschitz because the gauge is Lipschitz and uniformly bounded away from zero on the unit sphere. Its surface area formula gives the cone measure with factor x dot n. Central great-sphere directions have zero surface measure. This also independently verifies the closed-cap convention.

Ordinary sharp centroid Grünbaum then gives Gamma_d for EVERY through-source cap against one common boundary weight. Any containing cap contains the parallel through-source cap, and the positive weighted boundary measure is monotone. No comparison with the old unweighted cap volume is asserted.

## Actual erosion and uniform error

The sublevel g_K+epsilon f(1+a dot x)<=1 is a bounded convex body containing0 in its interior for all sufficiently small epsilon. It is nested in K because f is positive. On every ray, the defining derivative is at least1/R-epsilon C, so it is uniformly positive for small epsilon. The radial root exists uniquely between0 and the original radius. Its exact equation first gives uniform O(epsilon) displacement, and the Lipschitz bound for f then gives uniform O(epsilon^2) remainder in the stated linear expansion.

The same radial remainder bounds every hemisphere integral by the full sphere's area times that bound. Thus the O(epsilon^2) constant is independent of the cap normal. The first loss coefficient is exactly d times the projective image cap volume, and the total coefficient is D=d|T_a K|>0. Nestedness extends the same lower loss estimate from a central cap to any cap containing the source. No differentiability of the boundary or gauge beyond the elementary radial bounds is used.

As a direct d=1 calibration, for K=[-L,R] the normalizing coefficient is a=(R-L)/(2LR). Both weighted endpoint masses equal2LR/(L+R), their sum is D=4LR/(L+R), and each ray pays exactly Gamma_1 D. This checks the dimension-one normalization and first loss coefficient independently.

## Fixed closed covers: no coarea regularity required

The updated Section3 uses the stronger and simpler direct argument suggested during this audit. Normalize each source's total loss derivative to1. A FIXED assigned cap containing its source loses at least epsilon Gamma_d-O(epsilon^2) in that fiber, uniformly in its orientation. Other nested erosions can only remove additional captured mass. A pure-integer cap contains the whole source fiber, so pays epsilon+O(epsilon^2). Its original closed boundary mass is retained exactly.

The fixed selected covers continue to cover their base planes (and in particular all shrunken fibers); the slack cover masses only decrease. Total mass is M-m epsilon+O(epsilon^2), giving the printed normalized upper bound

    beta+epsilon(m beta-Gamma_d)/M+O(epsilon^2).

Hence beta<Gamma_d/m gives strict decrease. No cap response equalization, proper coarea assumption or supporting-face allocation is necessary here. Positivity of the source's interior persists under the explicit gauge sublevel construction.

The strict finite-extreme inclusion criterion is sufficient for simultaneous compatibility. Each changed support differs by at most delta/3; both target and weighted source supports may move, with total error at most2delta/3, leaving a positive margin. Every non-extreme representation follows by support linearity. The proof correctly avoids the one-fiber input-or-target shortcut when several fibers move.

For the lower-rank realization, the integer direction space is rational. Its orthogonal projection matrix has rational entries, so the projected integer lattice is discrete. A complementary ball smaller than its least nonzero projected norm adds no integer base, and points on the original integer affine span have complementary component0, so their fibers are unchanged. The relative hull plus that ball has full ambient interior. This is an actual realization of the perturbed prescribed fiber family; a local-minimum argument must, as usual, use that canonical family or explicitly assume such an actual local variation.

No substantive repair requested. The ordinary theorem supersedes the shape and cap-direction restrictions of the earlier free-simplex argument. Active anchored contact compatibility remains a separate unsolved interface, exactly as the sources state.
